module.typosquatting.checks: Generates variants of the domain name (typos, neighbouring letters, Unicode homoglyphs, hyphens, other extensions), finds the registered ones and classifies them: defensive domain of the owner, parking, or risk (recent, active mail, homoglyph).
module.typosquatting.fix:
Sort the look-alike domains listed in the finding: those you already own (defensive), legitimate namesakes unrelated to you, and risky ones (registered less than 90 days ago, with active mail or Unicode homoglyphs).
For each risky domain, identify the holder, registrar and host with WHOIS or RDAP (snippet), and see what it serves without opening it in your usual browser: use a urlscan.io scan or an isolated workstation.
If a domain imitates your brand to deceive your customers (fake shop, phishing, spoofed emails), report the abuse to its host and its registrar with screenshots, dates and links, then to Google Safe Browsing to get the page blocked.
If the holder acts in bad faith and your brand is protected, start a dispute resolution procedure: UDRP (for example through WIPO) for generic extensions, or the procedure of the extension's registry (Afnic for .fr). Keep the proof of your rights and of the abusive use.
Register the most likely variants yourself (common typos, main extensions) with your registrar, with automatic renewal. If they are not used for mail, neutralise their mail setup: null MX, SPF `v=spf1 -all` and DMARC `p=reject` (DNS snippet).
Protect your own domain against email spoofing: publish SPF, DKIM and a DMARC `p=reject`. This does not block a neighbouring domain, which has its own records: tell your customers and teams to check the sender's exact address.
Keep watching over time: run this scan regularly and enable an alert on new look-alike domains (brand or domain name monitoring service from your registrar, alerts on public Certificate Transparency certificates).
module.typosquatting.fix_snippet:
# WHOIS / RDAP
whois example.com
curl -sL https://rdap.org/domain/example.com
# DNS
example.net.         3600  IN  MX   0 .
example.net.         3600  IN  TXT  "v=spf1 -all"
_dmarc.example.net.  3600  IN  TXT  "v=DMARC1; p=reject"
module.typosquatting.title: Typosquatting
module.typosquatting.why: Registered domains almost identical to yours are used to phish your customers and to spoof your emails; spotting them lets you have them shut down or buy them back.
